The exogenously feeding tadpole phase is characterized by a protracted period of somatic growth that culminates in a dramatic body plan reorganization during the metamorphic climax. Adult body size in Alytes cisternasii is sexually dimorphic, with females attaining a greater ultimate snout-vent length than males.
